title: Ironforge
body: Ironforge is the ancient capital of the dwarves of Khaz Modan, carved deep into Ironforge Mountain above the snows of Dun Morogh. When the first dwarves came out of Uldaman, they raised an altar to the titan Khaz'goroth and built the Great Forge, and the city grew in rings of stone around that molten heart and took its name from it. From the High Seat beside the forge, King Magni Bronzebeard rules, though the senators of his court do not always welcome the reach of royal authority. The city has endured a great deal: the War of the Three Hammers, which drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from its gates, and the Horde siege of the Second War, which it held out against. Since the fall of Gnomeregan, the exiled gnomes of High Tinker Mekkatorque have made a home in Tinker Town, beside the Deeprun Tram their engineers designed to reach Stormwind. In the Hall of Explorers, the Explorers' League seeks proof that the dwarves were made by the titans.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ironforge (founding after leaving Uldaman, altar to Khaz'goroth and the Great Forge, city named for the forge, War of the Three Hammers, Second War siege held out, gnome refuge and Tinker Town, Deeprun Tram)

Senate line softened: quest 291 shows one senator's anger, not a habit. Rest verified against wiki Ironforge. Faction 0. Check: Javad 23127 spawned in Ironforge (guid 1815, phase 1, no event), added patch 2.1.0 per wiki.

parts.body: In recent years the draenei, exiles from another world who came to Azeroth aboard the Exodar, have joined the Alliance, and one of them now serves in Ironforge. On the northern side of the Great Forge, Farseer Javad teaches the shamans of his people, reminding each of them always to show respect for the elements of the world and the balance their spirits keep.

title: The Forlorn Cavern
body: Beyond the Mystic Ward, a long, dim road winds around an underground lake: the Forlorn Cavern, the corner of Ironforge where honest dwarves seldom linger. Its darkness and seclusion suit those whose business does not bear the light of the forges. Rogues keep a hall here, a shady dealer lounges on its outer stair, and warlocks teach their art in the shop of Gerrig Bonegrip. Bonegrip himself collects old and dangerous lore, the kind said to open doorways and wake things that sleep, and will not even speak the names of the relics he seeks for fear of listening ears. Not all is sinister: a fishing master and his supplier work the cavern's quiet waters.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Forlorn_Cavern (road around underground lake, between Mystic Ward and Hall of Explorers, shady deals, rogue and warlock trainers, Bonegrip's shop, Traveling Fisherman)

title: King Magni Bronzebeard
body: Magni Bronzebeard, eldest of three royal brothers, rules the dwarves of Khaz Modan from the High Seat beside the Great Forge. He held Ironforge through the Horde's siege in the Second War, pledged his people to the Alliance that freed Khaz Modan, and turned dwarven industry toward archaeology, helping to found the Explorers' League. Grief has followed him. When his brother Muradin was lost in Northrend, Magni poured his sorrow into forging the Ashbringer. His daughter, Princess Moira, vanished in the Burning Steppes while in the care of a dwarf named Kharan Mighthammer, and though the king's men turned the Steppes upside down, he feared she might be dead.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Magni_Bronzebeard (eldest of three brothers, Siege of Ironforge, Alliance pledge, Explorers' Guild, Ashbringer forged after Muradin's believed death, Moira)
quest 12771 description and reward text (eager to take the fight to Northrend, war priests, Muradin you must live)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/A_Desperate_Alliance (12771 and 12809 belong to the 3.0.2 Scourge Invasion chain, later removed)
quest 4341 description (Kharan watching over her, men turned the Steppes upside down, she could be dead)
notes: Converted: Thaurissan as Moira's captor moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 4362, whose description reveals the spell; 4361's turn-in only shows the fist slam); the opening now says only that she vanished in Kharan's care, as quest 4341 tells it. Moira's declaration and Magni's verdict added as part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4363) so his own entry follows his daughter's fate. The Scourge Invasion vow moved to part 3 (minState 13, no trigger): it comes from the removed 3.0.2 quest 12771, Wrath pre-launch content. Faction 1: template 55 hostile to Horde. Check: part 3 wording follows the 12771 reward text (you must live), not certainty; kept as Wrath-era history (12771 and its lead-in 12753 have no starter in 3.3.5, but their texts and Magni as ender remain in the database).

parts.body: Word from Kharan, a prisoner in Blackrock Depths, made the king slam his fist down in anger. His old adversary, Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, held Moira under a spell, and through her held Ironforge itself at his mercy. Magni's command was plain: kill the emperor to break the enchantment, and do the princess no harm, whatever she might say or do.

Thaurissan fell, but Moira was not freed as her father had hoped. She mourned the emperor and sent word that the heir to Ironforge would be a Dark Iron dwarf, whether Magni approved or not. Visibly shaken, the king slumped into his throne to brood over it, concluding that even in death, Thaurissan had won.

When the Scourge struck at the capitals on the eve of the war in Northrend, a holy artifact charged with the Light of the naaru was carried to Ironforge. Magni vowed to send the necropolises scurrying back to Northrend with his people right behind them, and swore by the honor of the Bronzebeards to find Muradin, crying out that his brother must still live.
sources: quest 12771 description and reward text (artifact, necropolises back to Northrend, Muradin you must live)

title: High Tinker Mekkatorque
body: Gelbin Mekkatorque first won fame in Gnomeregan as an inventor, and gnomish voters raised him to be High Tinker, leader of their people. He trusted his friend and chief advisor, Sicco Thermaplugg, and that trust undid them all. When troggs broke into Gnomeregan, a desperate measure Thermaplugg urged poisoned the city instead and killed most of its people, and Thermaplugg stayed behind to rule the ruins, a king of nothing. Mekkatorque led the survivors to Ironforge, where King Magni granted them refuge, and from Tinker Town he plans the day Gnomeregan will be retaken. The first step, he says, is the death of the betrayer.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gelbin_Mekkatorque (inventor, elected High Tinker, Thermaplugg chief advisor, trogg invasion, gas killed about eighty percent, refuge in Ironforge, Tinker Town)
quest 2929 description (betrayal, king of nothing, we will retake Gnomeregan)
quest 12809 description and reward text (Light-infused artifact, turn dusk into dawn)

The naaru artifact sentence moved to part 2 (minState 13, no trigger): removed 3.0.2 Scourge Invasion quest 12809, Wrath pre-launch content. npc_text 15863 reread: only 'Welcome to Tinker Town!', nothing rests on it. No Operation: Gnomeregan part: no 3.3.5 text or quest in Ironforge supports it (Dun Morogh 106 tells the preparations). Faction 1: template 64 hostile to Horde. Check: betrayal confirmed as setup (2929 offer, also 2904 reward text); part 2 kept as Wrath-era history on the same basis as 153702 part 3 (12809 and lead-in 12808 have no starter in 3.3.5).

parts.body: Mekgineer Thermaplugg has been slain in the depths of Gnomeregan. The High Tinker, who once called him friend, takes a grim pleasure in the news and likes to imagine that the last thing to pass through the traitor's head was a boot. With Thermaplugg dead, he declares, the plan to retake Gnomeregan has come one step closer to being real.

When the Scourge struck at the capitals on the eve of the war in Northrend, a holy artifact charged with the Light of the naaru was carried to Tinker Town. Mekkatorque was enchanted. Such a store of Light, he said, could power a device to turn dusk into dawn, and destroy the Scourge with a single pull of a lever.
sources: quest 12809 description and reward text (Light-infused artifact, turn dusk into dawn, one pull of a lever)

title: Royal Historian Archesonus
body: Royal Historian Archesonus keeps the memory of Ironforge from his place in the royal chamber, a few steps from the king's throne, and welcomes anyone who wishes to learn the history of the city. His favorite tale, and his most urgent, is that of the Dark Iron dwarves: the proud city of Thaurissan, the explosion that turned its green country into the Burning Steppes, and the nation that rose again from the ashes. His interest is not only scholarly. Dark Irons are surfacing more and more often, raising fortresses in the Badlands, digging in Uldaman and even striking at the dwarven dam on Loch Modan, and Archesonus seeks adventurers to learn what the ruins of Thaurissan still hide.
sources: npc_text 2234, 2236, 2237, 2238, 2239 (gossip history of Thaurissan and recent Dark Iron activity)
DB spawn: Archesonus 8879 at map 38.4,55.3, beside Magni 2784 at 39.1,56.2
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide and nothing from a later era. The history is his gossip and the premise of quests 3702 and 3701; npc_text 2234 to 2239 reread, classic texts. verified

title: High Explorer Magellas
body: High Explorer Magellas heads the Explorers' League from the Hall of Explorers, home to the league's library and a museum of wonders gathered across the world: an astrolabe crafted by the highborne of drowned Suramar, an unknown pteradon skeleton from Un'Goro Crater, a Horde catapult left from the Second War, and etched reliefs from Uldaman that tie the dwarves to the golem-like earthen. Proving that the dwarves were shaped by the titans is the league's great ambition. Magellas is a busy dwarf with little time to spare, but for anything of grave importance to the league he is all ears.
sources: quest 2279 reward text (find of the century, enchanted creation)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Explorers'_League (Hall of Explorers headquarters, Magellas heads the hall)
quest 2279 completion text (very busy, all ears for grave importance)
notes: Converted: the miniature discs and the find of the century moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2279); his hopes for Uldum and the search for the plates moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2964). Opening now ends on his manner from the 2279 completion text. Faction 1: template 55.

parts.body: Out of Uldaman came a miniature copy of the Discs of Norgannon, a titan record of how the Creators made the earthen. Magellas could scarcely believe what he heard and hailed it as the find of the century, perhaps the very key that would prove once and for all the dwarves' enchanted creation, and set the league to study it.

The discs led the league to the sealed gates of Uldum in Tanaris, but they proved to be only part of a set, and without the Plates of Uldum the gates stay closed. Magellas has agreed to put the venture on hold until research narrows down where the plates lie hidden. Uldum, he promises, beckons.

title: Historian Karnik
body: Historian Karnik tends the books of the Explorers' League in the Hall of Explorers, glad to help any seeker whose answers can be found in print, though he has no time for meaningless questions. With his friend, the prospector Hammertoe Grez, he has long searched for the lost artifacts of Uldaman and the origins of the dwarves, while the Shadowforge clan of the Dark Iron dwarves digs in the same ruins. Lately his studies reach far beyond Khaz Modan, as far as the elven ruins of Azshara, which his companion Tymor has offered to help him investigate.
sources: quests 723, 724 (Hammertoe's death, Karnik his partner in seeking Uldaman's artifacts)
quests 725, 726, 762 (Belgrum, king's authority, Angor Fortress, Ambassador Infernus sent by Ragnaros)
quest 1139 description and reward text (Tablet of Will)

notes: Converted: Hammertoe's death moved from the opening to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 724, the end of the Badlands chain at Karnik, unused by badlands.json); Belgrum's order and the plan to strike Angor Fortress to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 726); Infernus and his destruction to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 762; badlands.json uses ACCEPT 762 and KILL 2745, not this); the Tablet of Will to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 1139). The opening no longer tells Hammertoe's fate, which is the Badlands' story (entries 316, 326). npc_text 6383 reread, a classic text. Faction 1: template 55. Check: Valley of the Watchers clue dropped from the opening (it is the Uldum lead that 153714 part 3 reveals); part 3 says Infernus watched over the Shadowforge rather than commanded them, as quest 762 and badlands.json 306 have it.

parts.body: Hammertoe is dead, taken by the Shadowforge, who had learned how much he and Karnik knew. His amulet, his life's work, came to Karnik with word of his end, and the historian set his grief aside: if Hammertoe sent the amulet, he understood what was at stake, and the mourning would have to wait.

Karnik sent word of the threat to Advisor Belgrum, whose eyes widened at the note. On the king's authority he ordered Karnik to act swiftly and decisively and halt the Shadowforge in the Badlands. Karnik knew where to strike: their work in Uldaman could be slowed by a blow at their base of operations, Angor Fortress.

At Angor Fortress the Shadowforge were watched over by Ambassador Infernus, sent by Ragnaros himself to mind their search for lost artifacts. In time the ambassador was destroyed, and Belgrum sent word of the victory to Karnik and promised to send aid to the Badlands to recover the excavation site.

Cut off from Blackrock Spire, the Shadowforge were slowed, but Hammertoe's dream was still unfulfilled: the Tablet of Will, a titan shard said to give created beings a will of their own. Brought back from Uldaman at Belgrum's request, it left the advisor shaking his head in disbelief, and he sent it to the king's mages to learn whether the legends are true.
sources: quest 1139 description, completion and reward text

title: Prospector Stormpike
body: Prospector Stormpike works in the Explorers' League headquarters in the Hall of Explorers, a hot-tempered dwarf who cannot abide trivial matters or slow progress. Yet scholars as far off as Southshore send him their puzzles, for there may be no one north of Blackrock Spire better at breaking ciphers and untangling enchanted script. He keeps a close eye on the league's digs, from Prospector Ironband's excavation in Loch Modan, whose missing shipment of blastpowder enraged him, to Uldaman, lost to a sudden tide of troggs. When his friend Baelog and a small band of dwarves were cut off deep inside that dig, Stormpike sent for help to find them.
sources: quest 301 description and reward text (hotheaded, Ironband's blastpowder)
quest 514 description (no one north of Blackrock Spire who can read this)

title: Tinkmaster Overspark
body: Tinkmaster Overspark calls himself the chief architect of modern gnomish engineering, and from Tinker Town he guards the bold principles of that craft so that gnomish invention may keep shining brighter than any other. The fall of Gnomeregan cost him dearly. His creation Techbot, once a kindly helper full of gizmos and knowledge, was jolted by a stray spark as the city fell; its positronic brain turned negatronic, reversing its nature, and it now roams the ruined halls in a frenzy. Overspark longs to recover its memory core and set it right. He also mentions, almost in passing, that he would welcome any good schematic for eliminating radiation.
sources: npc_text 2137 (chief architect, arclight spanners, schematic for radiation elimination)
quest 2923 description (Techbot once kind and helpful)
creature_template 7944 subname Gnomish Engineering Trainer, faction 64

Changed admits with some embarrassment to mentions almost in passing, matching npc_text 2137. Faction 1: template 64.

parts.body: Techbot's memory core has come back to Tinker Town at last. Overspark is overjoyed and sets to work at once to learn what polarized his creation's brain, murmuring to the poor machine not to fret, that it will be fixed, even as he hunts his bench for a misplaced plug for one of his spanners.

title: Talvash del Kissel
body: Talvash del Kissel calls himself a jeweler of great renown in Ironforge, or former renown, for the chicanery of a competitor has sullied his good name, and a bad reputation in his trade spells ruin. Without a copper to spare, the gnome scrapes by in a small house in the city, greeting strangers with nervous denials: if they have come about fee collection or a summons, they must have the wrong gnome. Information, he insists, is never free. Yet he still swears that one day, out of the hole he is so unjustly in, he will make the finest trinkets in all of Azeroth.
sources: quest 2948 reward text (unjustly in a hole)

parts.body: The shattered necklace marked with the initials TdK is his, one of his finest pieces, made for a paladin bent on clearing an evil taint from Uldaman. The paladin died there, and the rival spread word that the necklace had cursed him. Find its three missing gems, Talvash offers, and he will restore it, so long as the world hears that he does not make cursed jewelry.
sources: quest 2199 reward text (paladin died in Uldaman)
quest 2200 description (rumor of the curse, the deal)

parts.body: The gems were found where the dead paladin's journal said, among the Shadowforge, the troggs and their elder, and a power source was torn from the mightiest construct in Uldaman. Talvash fused them into the necklace and handed it over gladly, asking only that its wearer tell everyone, loudly and often, who made it, and that it is not cursed.

title: A King's Tribute
body: Among the soldiers lost in the Thandol Span tragedy was a dwarf named Sully Balloo. He was found pinned beneath the icy waters, and his last letter, written with painstaking care and addressed to a Mrs. Sara Balloo of Ironforge, survived the water and the war, though its envelope dissolves at a touch, leaving only a few pages that begin 'My dear Sara'. Whoever holds those pages now has a fallen soldier's last errand to finish: carrying his final words home to her.
sources: quest 637 description and reward text (waterlogged letter, pinned beneath the icy waters)
quest 686 description (Magni, every dwarf that fights for the Alliance, commission to Marblesten)
quest 689 description (Thandol Span tragedy, Alterac Granite from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad)
gameobject 139852 Memorial to Sully Balloo spawned in Ironforge
notes: Converted: Sara's grief moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 637); her plea and the king's commission to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 686, offered once the plea is delivered); the granite and the finished memorial to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 700). Sully's death stays in the opening: it is the premise of 637, found with the letter. wetlands.json 1110 also names Sully and the memorial (not this file's to change). creature_text 2695, 2784, 2790 reread: nothing from later builds. Check: dropped 'does not yet know' from the opening, which part 1 would make untrue.

parts.body: The letter broke Sara's heart. She begged to hear it was not so, read Sully's pages one by one, and cried out against the unfairness of it, calling for her dearest Sully to come back to her, and asking why anyone would bring her such news.

Too stricken to stand before the throne herself, Sara sent a plea to King Magni. The king, who feels the loss of every dwarf who falls for the Alliance, could not bring Sully back from the Twisting Nether, but he could honor him, and he commissioned a memorial from Grand Mason Marblesten of the Royal Stonecutters Union.

Marblesten would work only with the finest stone, Alterac granite from Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad, quarried from war-torn Lordaeron. The finished memorial now stands in Ironforge. To the king it seems a small token beside a great dwarf's life, but he hopes it will remind those who come after for whom such soldiers gave their lives.
sources: gameobject 139852 Memorial to Sully Balloo spawned in Ironforge

title: The Ruin of Thaurissan
body: Royal Historian Archesonus tells the history of the Dark Iron dwarves. Hundreds of years ago, while the dwarven nation was torn by civil war, the Dark Iron capital of Thaurissan stood proudly in a lush land then part of the Redridge Mountains. A colossal explosion consumed it, leaving the city in ruin and the country around it the ashen waste now called the Burning Steppes. How it happened, the historian admits, no one knows. The survivors withdrew into the mountain and rebuilt; from the ashes rose Blackrock Spire, a new Dark Iron nation, fortifications in the Cauldron of the Searing Gorge, and rumors of an ancient evil ruling the kingdom. Now the Dark Irons are stirring again, and Archesonus sends helpers into the smoldering ruins to learn what the relics can reveal, past the assassins who guard them.
sources: quest 3701 description and reward text (relics, Thaurissan guardians)
notes: Trimmed for length only (147 to 138 words, the new Story range). Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide and nothing from a later era. The whole history is Archesonus's telling (quest 3702 and its gossip); the 3701 turn-in reveals nothing specific beyond that the relics explain much. verified. Cause of the explosion left as unknown, attributed to the historian, which matches npc_text 2237; wiki Ragnaros account deliberately not used.

title: The Princess and the Emperor
body: Moira Bronzebeard, King Magni's daughter, vanished in the Burning Steppes while in the care of a dwarf named Kharan Mighthammer, the pitiful lout, in the king's words, who was supposed to be watching over her. Magni has had his men turn the Steppes upside down, and they found a single clue: she may be somewhere inside Blackrock Depths, where Kharan himself is said to be held prisoner. For all the king knows, his daughter may already be dead. Sobbing on his throne, he wants Kharan found, and he wants answers.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 4341. Thaurissan's spell and Magni's order moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 4362; 4361's turn-in shows only the fist slam); Moira's mourning and the Dark Iron heir to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 4363, from Moira after the emperor's death); Magni's verdict to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 4363). All quests Alliance only; 4342 and the start of 4363 lie in Blackrock Depths, which has no file.

parts.body: Kharan's tale, carried back to Ironforge, made the king slam his fist down in anger. Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, Magni's old adversary, held Moira under a spell, and through her held the kingdom itself at his mercy. Magni's command was plain: kill the emperor to break the enchantment, and do the princess no harm, for whatever she said or did would be Thaurissan's doing.

When Thaurissan fell, Moira did not rejoice. She wept over the emperor, called him a great and honorable dwarf, and blamed his killers for ruining her life and the life of her unborn child. Her message for her father was defiant: the heir to the Kingdom of Ironforge would be a Dark Iron dwarf, whether he approved or not.

The news left King Magni visibly upset. He rewarded those who had served him from the royal vault, then slumped into his throne to mull over the bizarre turn of events, concluding that even in death, Thaurissan had won.

title: The Exiles of Gnomeregan
body: In Tinker Town the gnomes of Gnomeregan live as exiles, and nearly every one of them carries a piece of the catastrophe. High Tinker Mekkatorque trusted Mekgineer Thermaplugg, who betrayed him and all gnomekind and now rules the ruined city; the High Tinker wants the betrayer dead as the first step toward taking Gnomeregan back. Master Mechanic Castpipe frets over the vital data left behind in the flight and organizes missions to pull it from the city's high security terminals. Tinkmaster Overspark grieves for his creation Techbot, turned against its makers, and Klockmort Spannerspan needs the essential artificials no one remembered to save. Gnoarn, bald since the radiation leak and furious at the troggs, directs scouts and an underground assault crew from central command in Ironforge.
sources: quest 2927 description and reward text (Gnoarn's hair, radiation leak, troggs)
quests 2039, 2041 descriptions (Bingles reconnaissance, Shoni's underground assault crew, central command)
creature_queststarter: 7937 starts 2929, 7950 starts 2930, 7944 starts 2922, 6169 starts 2924, 6569 starts 2927, 2039, 2041
notes: Converted: the opening is unchanged, since every thread in it is a premise told on offering. Outcomes added as parts in rising order: the data (QUEST_DONE 2930), Techbot's core (QUEST_DONE 2922), the artificials (QUEST_DONE 2924), Thermaplugg's death (QUEST_DONE 2929). Gnoarn's threads end in Loch Modan (Bingles, 2039) and Stormwind (Shoni, 2041) and are left to those files. ACCEPT 2927 is shared with dun_morogh.json 134, a known old overlap, left as is. All quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Castpipe has his data. A band went deep into Gnomeregan, worked its way up through the lower security terminals one punch card at a time, and brought back the prismatic punch card from the high security terminal. The master mechanic was overjoyed, swearing the gnomes could not have gone another moment without what it holds.
Techbot's memory core has been carried out of Gnomeregan to Tinker Town. Overspark set to work on it at once, determined to find what polarized his creation's brain and to put the poor machine right.

Klockmort Spannerspan has his essential artificials at last, pulled from the artificial extrapolators in the deep halls of the city, and can begin the new experiments he had planned. Such bravery, he says, has advanced gnomish research by leaps and bounds.

Mekgineer Thermaplugg has been slain in the depths of his stolen city. The High Tinker relishes the news, hoping the last thing to pass through the betrayer's head was a boot, and declares that with Thermaplugg dead, the exiles are one step closer to retaking Gnomeregan.

title: Secrets of the Creators
body: The Explorers' League has long suspected that the dwarves were not born but made, shaped by the titans like the earthen of old. Uldaman in the Badlands lies at the heart of that search, but the dig there was lost when troggs came so fast and in such numbers that not even dwarven might could stop them. Prospector Stormpike fears that some of his people are trapped behind enemy lines. His friend Baelog led a small band of dwarves deep within the site just before the troggs showed up, and if Baelog and his company still live, Stormpike wants them found.
sources: quest 2240 description and reward text (Chamber of Khaz'mul)

parts.body: Baelog and his band were alive, stuck deep in the ruins and passing the time with a wager over Olaf's beard. Baelog's journal told the way into a secret vault behind a huge locked door, the Chamber of Khaz'mul, and since his band could not leave, others would have to explore it for them and report to Stormpike.

Deeper in, a stone watcher kept the Discs of Norgannon, where the Creators' making of the earthen is chronicled, and the discs yielded a miniature copy of themselves. High Explorer Magellas declared it the find of the century, perhaps the proof of the dwarves' enchanted creation the league had always sought.

Historian Karnik went further. The Creators were rumored to keep other repositories across Azeroth, and his clues pointed to Uldum, behind the sealed gates of the Valley of the Watchers in Tanaris. No one could say what the miniature discs would do there, only that they had to be tried.

Before the gates of Uldum the discs hummed and glowed, and another stone watcher sprang to life, a guardian of entry. The discs alone were not enough, it said: the Plates of Uldum must be joined to them before anyone may enter.

Back in Ironforge, Karnik likened the discs to keys on a ring, of which the plates are the missing ones. Where they lie, no one knows, and the league has set the search aside until research narrows down where they might be hidden. Uldum, Magellas promises, still beckons.
